verificationLog.notes: Replaced Gemini 3.6 Flash with Gemini 3.7 Flash across the catalog, Google provider default/task routing, managed-cloud canonicalization, and the economy tier list. Official Google documentation confirms the exact gemini-3.7-flash API ID, 1,048,576-token input and 65,536-token output limits, text/image/audio/video/PDF input with text-only output, function calling, code execution, search grounding, context caching, batch, computer use (preview), and low/medium/high thinking levels — minimal is NOT supported on 3.7, so it was dropped from supportedEfforts. Pricing is the current promotional rate of $0.75/M input, $3.75/M output, $0.075/M cache read, which Google lists as reverting to $1.50/$7.50/$0.15 on 2027-01-01 and must be re-verified before that date. Benchmarks are omitted because Google publishes none for 3.7 and carrying 3.6 numbers forward would be fabricated. openrouter.ai/api/v1/models confirms the google/gemini-3.7-flash slug. Sources retrieved 2026-08-18: ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models, /docs/models/gemini-3.7-flash, /docs/pricing, and openrouter.ai/api/v1/models.

Added OpenRouter's current ByteDance Seedance 2.5 video route from the live official video-model catalog and current create, poll, authenticated-content, and signed-webhook documentation. The canonical record carries every supported 4-30 second duration, each exact resolution/aspect/pixel tuple, audio and seed support, and the provider-published video-token formula so reservation cost is derived from pixels rather than a misleading flat resolution rate. The managed adapter polls and downloads authenticated content into AGI private storage; provider URLs never become client output. Sources retrieved 2026-08-10: openrouter.ai/api/v1/videos/models, openrouter.ai/docs/guides/overview/multimodal/video-generation, and the OpenRouter video API reference.

Reverified current Qwen pricing against Alibaba Cloud Model Studio and tied catalog prices to the deployment scope the production adapter actually calls. The canonical Qwen adapter defaults to dashscope.aliyuncs.com, the Chinese-mainland deployment, not dashscope-intl.aliyuncs.com. In that scope qwen3.5-flash uses three input-length bands: $0.029/$0.287 through 128K input, $0.115/$1.147 above 128K through 256K, and $0.172/$1.72 above 256K through 1M. qwen3.7-plus uses $0.276/$1.101 through 256K and $0.826/$3.301 above 256K through 1M; the former International-scope $0.40/$1.60 and $1.20/$4.80 values did not match the production endpoint and were removed. Implicit cache reads cost 20% of the active input band and explicit cache creation costs 125%, so every band carries its matching cache rates. Limited-time discounts remain excluded. Sources retrieved 2026-08-10: alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/model-pricing and alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/context-cache. The pricing page identifies qwen3.5-flash as the current alias of the 2026-02-23 snapshot and qwen3.7-plus as the current alias of the 2026-05-26 snapshot.

Reverified the complete current OpenAI reasoning family against each official model page, the official GPT-5.6 model guidance, and the founder-provided official comparison screenshot. The published short-context rates were already correct: Sol $5 input / $0.50 cached input / $30 output, Terra $2 / $0.20 / $12, and Luna $0.20 / $0.02 / $1.20 per million tokens. All three publish a 1,050,000-token context window, 128,000 maximum output, and a 2026-02-16 knowledge cutoff. The cards do not publish a separate 922,000 maximum-input limit, so that previously derived field was removed rather than presented as an upstream fact. Requests above 272,000 input tokens are charged at 2x input and 1.5x output; the missing Terra and Luna long-context blocks are restored from those published multipliers, including the family's 1.25x cache-write rate. Image input supports low, high, original, and auto detail. Provider-hosted tools remain separate from AGI application capability flags: catalog search is true only because the Responses search harness is implemented, while computer use, code execution, and image generation stay false until their AGI execution paths are wired and verified. Sources retrieved 2026-08-10: developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-sol, developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-terra, developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.6-luna, and developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/latest-model.

Corrected the stable internal runway-gen-4 catalog entry from the image-to-video-only gen4_turbo wire model to Runway's current text-to-video-capable gen4.5 model. Runway announced Gen-4.5 in December 2025; its POST /v1/text_to_video reference accepts gen4.5 but not gen4_turbo, constrains prompts to 1-1,000 UTF-16 code units, supports only 1280:720 landscape and 720:1280 portrait output, and accepts integer durations from 2-10 seconds. Runway prices gen4.5 at 12 credits per output second and sells credits for $0.01 each, so canonical cost is $0.12/second for the supported 720p orientations. The separate API changelog dates Gen-4.5 API availability to 2026-02-10; that API date is not the model release date. Removed the prior invented 4,000-token context because Runway documents a character limit, not a token context window. Documentation availability is not account provisioning: the entry remains availability=unavailable and Runway has no provider default until a live AGI-owned account probe returns 200. Runway also requires successful task output URLs to be downloaded and stored because they expire after 24-48 hours and must not be exposed directly. Sources retrieved 2026-08-09: docs.dev.runwayml.com/api, docs.dev.runwayml.com/assets/inputs, docs.dev.runwayml.com/guides/models, docs.dev.runwayml.com/guides/pricing, docs.dev.runwayml.com/api-details/api_changelog, and docs.dev.runwayml.com/assets/outputs.

Founder flagged that gpt-4o-mini-tts carries a Deprecated badge on the developers.openai.com model catalog listing — correct, and it landed the same day we adopted it. Resolved against four sources: the listing badges it Deprecated; its own model page shows NO deprecation banner and no shutdown date; the deprecations table has no family-level row for it (only snapshot gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-03-20 -> -2025-12-15, shut down 2026-07-23); and the text-to-speech guide still calls it the newest and most reliable TTS model. Decisive fact: it is the ONLY model OpenAI serves on /v1/audio/speech — gpt-audio-1.5's model page lists "Speech generation | v1/audio/speech | Not supported". So there is no newer member of this family to move to. Marked deprecated:true (compile.mjs then sets selectable:false) and KEPT, because removing it would leave the OpenAI TTS path with no model at all. NOT ADDED, deliberately: the realtime family (gpt-realtime-2.1, gpt-realtime-2.1-mini, gpt-realtime-translate, gpt-realtime-whisper). Three reasons — ModelType has no "realtime" member, so it is a schema change across the TS union, the registry schema and both Rust registries; we ship no duplex audio path (founder-gated on a realtime provider plus echo cancellation); and registering them live would advertise capability we do not have. Recorded as VOICE-REALTIME-FAMILY-ABSENT so the ids do not need re-researching: gpt-realtime-2.1 ($4/$24 text, $32/$64 audio, $0.40 cached, 128k ctx, 32k max out) and gpt-realtime-2.1-mini ($0.60/$2.40 text, $10/$20 audio) are the current heads; gpt-realtime, gpt-realtime-mini, gpt-audio, gpt-audio-mini and every gpt-4o-audio/gpt-4o-realtime variant shut down 2027-01-20. gpt-4o-transcribe and gpt-4o-mini-transcribe carry NO deprecated badge and stay as-is.

Added the two OpenRouter router routes the product had no entry for: openrouter/auto (Auto Router) and openrouter/free (Free Models Router), and set open_router.defaultModel to openrouter/auto, which was previously empty so the provider had no route at all. Every field is read from https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models retrieved 2026-08-29 with a live key. Auto Router: canonical_slug openrouter/auto, 2,000,000 context, tokenizer "Router", modality text+image+file+audio+video->text+image, and supported_parameters including reasoning, reasoning_effort, tools, tool_choice and structured_outputs — hence reasoning.control "effort". Free Models Router: canonical_slug openrouter/free, 200,000 context, modality text+image->text, pricing prompt "0" and completion "0", and supported_parameters including reasoning_effort, tools and structured_outputs. Both routes report pricing that is resolved per request — auto returns "-1" for prompt and completion because cost follows the model it selects, so no per-million rate is recorded here and reservation must price the resolved route, not the router. No benchmarks are recorded because OpenRouter publishes none for either router, and carrying a member model's numbers forward would be fabricated. openrouter/auto is recorded with inputCost/outputCost 0 because ModelMetadata requires both and the router publishes no rate of its own; managed metering must price the model the router actually resolved (the completion response reports it) rather than the router record, so this route is safe on BYOK — where OpenRouter bills the key holder directly — and must not be exposed on a metered managed plan until resolved-route pricing is wired. openrouter/free is genuinely zero-rated ("0"/"0" from the provider).

Both router routes were exercised end to end against the live API after the account key was rotated. openrouter/auto returned HTTP 200 in 752ms and reported routing to deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731, confirming the earlier note that the router itself publishes no rate and that metering must price the resolved model. openrouter/free returned HTTP 200 and routed to free members (nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free, minimax/minimax-m2.7:free) with usage.cost 0, confirming the zero rating. Both free members are reasoning models whose reasoning tokens count against max_tokens: a 16-token cap returned empty content while a 200-token cap returned the expected text with finish_reason "stop" and 31 reasoning tokens. The product default is DEFAULT_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS 8192, so this is not reachable in normal use, but any caller that lowers the cap for a free-router turn must leave room for reasoning tokens.

gemini-embedding-2.name: Gemini Embedding 2
gemini-embedding-2.pricingNote: Standard text input $0.20/M tokens; Batch text input $0.10/M tokens. Image/audio/video prices vary by modality.

gemini-3.1-flash-image.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash Image
gemini-3.1-flash-image.pricingNote: Input $0.50/1M (text/image). Output $3.00/1M for text and thinking, $60.00/1M for images. Image output bills by resolution: 0.5K = 747 tokens ($0.045), 1K = 1120 tokens ($0.067), 2K = 1680 tokens ($0.101), 4K = 2520 tokens ($0.151). `imagePerImageCost` carries the 1K rate. CORRECTED 2026-08-06: this entry previously read inputCost 0.039 / outputCost 0 — 0.039 is the RETIRED gemini-2.5-flash-image per-image rate sitting in a per-1M-token field, so every generation was metered at roughly a thousandth of cost and image output was billed as free. Sourced from the published Gemini API pricing table.

deepseek-v4-pro.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro
deepseek-v4-pro.pricingNote: DeepSeek made its 75% V4-Pro launch discount permanent on 2026-05-22: flat $0.435/$0.87 per 1M tokens, cache-read $0.003625. No post-promo reversion.

qwen-3.5-flash.name: Qwen 3.5 Flash
qwen-3.5-flash.pricingNote: Chinese-mainland list price per 1M tokens, matching the canonical dashscope.aliyuncs.com adapter endpoint: $0.029 input/$0.287 output through 128K input, $0.115/$1.147 above 128K through 256K, and $0.172/$1.72 above 256K through 1M. The recorded cache-read price is the automatic implicit-cache rate of 20% of input; explicit five-minute cache hits cost 10% and writes cost 125%.

runway-gen-4.name: Runway Gen-4.5
runway-gen-4.unavailableReason: Runway text-to-video provisioning has not been verified by a live AGI-owned account probe.
runway-gen-4.pricingNote: Runway Gen-4.5 text-to-video costs $0.12/second and supports only 1280:720 landscape or 720:1280 portrait output, with integer durations from 2-10 seconds. The model remains non-selectable until AGI verifies provider provisioning with a live 200 probe; default video routing stays on the verified Google Veo route.

seedance-2.5.name: ByteDance: Seedance 2.5
seedance-2.5.pricingNote: OpenRouter bills video tokens as width x height x 24 frames/second x duration / 1024. The current with-audio and without-audio video-token SKUs are both $0.0000107/token, so every reservation uses the exact catalog pixel tuple rather than a flat resolution price.

gpt-image-2.name: GPT Image 2
gpt-image-2.pricingNote: OpenAI image generation guide uses a calculator for gpt-image-2 output-token/cost estimation; common 1024x1024 estimates are $0.006 low, $0.053 medium, and $0.211 high.

gpt-4o-mini-tts.name: GPT-4o Mini TTS
gpt-4o-mini-tts.pricingNote: $0.60/1M input text tokens, $12/1M output audio tokens. Default snapshot gpt-4o-mini-tts-2025-12-15 (the 2025-03-20 snapshot shut down 2026-07-23). DEPRECATED on developers.openai.com's model catalog listing, but retained because it is the only model OpenAI serves on /v1/audio/speech — gpt-audio-1.5 explicitly does not support that endpoint, no successor is named in the deprecations table, no shutdown date is published, and the text-to-speech guide still calls it "our newest and most reliable text-to-speech model". The migration path OpenAI is signalling is audio-native chat (gpt-audio-1.5) and realtime (gpt-realtime-2.1), neither of which is a drop-in for a REST speech call. Verified 2026-07-28.

qwen-3.7-plus.name: Qwen 3.7 Plus
qwen-3.7-plus.pricingNote: Chinese-mainland list price per 1M tokens, matching the canonical dashscope.aliyuncs.com adapter endpoint: $0.276 input/$1.101 output through 256K input and $0.826/$3.301 above 256K through 1M. The recorded cache-read price is the automatic implicit-cache rate of 20% of input; explicit five-minute cache hits cost 10% and writes cost 125%. Limited-time discounts are intentionally excluded.

veo-3.1.name: Veo 3.1
veo-3.1.pricingNote: Veo 3.1 Standard with audio: $0.40/second at 720p or 1080p; $0.60/second at 4k. 1080p and 4k require 8-second generations.

veo-3.1-fast.name: Veo 3.1 Fast
veo-3.1-fast.pricingNote: Veo 3.1 Fast with audio: $0.10/second at 720p, $0.12/second at 1080p, $0.30/second at 4k. 1080p and 4k require 8-second generations. Verified against ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing on 2026-08-12.

gpt-4o-transcribe.name: GPT-4o Transcribe
gpt-4o-transcribe.pricingNote: $2.50/1M input, $10/1M output tokens; 16k context. Was $0.006 — whisper-1's per-minute rate left behind when whisper-1 was replaced, which inputCost (dollars per 1M tokens) understated by ~417x. Verified 2026-07-28 against developers.openai.com/api/docs/models.

gpt-4o-mini-transcribe.name: GPT-4o Mini Transcribe
gpt-4o-mini-transcribe.pricingNote: $1.25/1M input, $5/1M output tokens; 16k context. Default snapshot gpt-4o-mini-transcribe-2025-12-15. Was $0.006 — whisper-1's per-minute rate. Verified 2026-07-28 against developers.openai.com/api/docs/models.

veo-3.1-lite.name: Veo 3.1 Lite
veo-3.1-lite.pricingNote: Veo 3.1 Lite with audio: $0.05/second at 720p, $0.08/second at 1080p. 4k output is NOT supported on Lite. Paid tier only. Verified end to end against veo-3.1-lite-generate-preview on 2026-08-06 (200 + completed operation).

gemini-omni-flash-preview.name: Gemini Omni Flash
gemini-omni-flash-preview.pricingNote: Paid tier only (no free tier). Input $1.50/1M (text/image/video/audio); output $9.00/1M text and $17.50/1M video. Video output bills at 5,792 tokens per second of 720p, an effective ~$0.10 per second. Sourced from the published Gemini API pricing table, 2026-08-06.

gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview.name: Gemini 3.5 Live Translate
gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview.pricingNote: Low-latency real-time speech-to-speech translation, 70+ languages. Free tier is free of charge; paid tier $3.50/1M input and $21.00/1M output audio tokens, equivalently $0.0053/min in and $0.0315/min out. Audio bills at 25 tokens per second, an effective ~$0.0368 per minute. Sourced from the published Gemini API pricing table, 2026-08-06. INTERIM: adopted while OpenAI's live/realtime API is unreleased; revisit when that ships.
